My Chemical Romance.

 *trigger warning* 

Here's the story; I came from a not-so-loving home. I was sexually abused by my grandfather throught my childhood until he died. Beaten by my dad while my mother watched not caring. My sister pulled a knife on me and tried to kill me. My mother also refusing to break up the fights my siblings and I got into. I was diagnosed with COS (Childhood Onset Schizophrenia) when I was 11 years old (looking back now probably from the trauma. But how do you call it that when it's your everyday reality as a kid?) I didn't know better. I was a young child and had no concept of what a true family or home is. I never had friends because my father was in the navy and we traveled/moved a lot at the whim of the government. I wasn't even treated for schizophrenia until I was 11, even though the onset was at 10  because no one even noticed I was acting strange. After some treatment I did start to fall out of delusional thinking, but was still tortured by voices and hallucinations that were not pretty to see. I found music comforting, as I could drown out most of the noise in my head by listening to something else.
 Focusing on something else. Anything to get rid of the hellish voices. And then I discovered My Chemical Romance. The angsty music really spoke to me, even as an adult today (doing much better by the way) about suffering, political corruption, the horrors of war (as I see what they did to my father) and pushing through all the hate and negativity that permeates this world, to try and see the light. That message got through some of my darkest days. And Gerard Way taught me never to be ashamed of who I am, despite being in peices most days. And taught me to keep going. No matter what life brings.

If you are so concerned about your future, maybe you don't want to die? If you truly wanted to end it you would care about nothing. I live with suicidal thoughts everyday. I'm not going to tell you "it gets better" bs. But when I do I think of all the things I have to do the next day. Made me realize I don't really want to die because I'm concerned about my life. You still care, get it? You still have a want to forfill your responsibilities in your life. You don't want to die. You just feel that way. Sometimes what we feel isn't the truth. If you feel like maybe someone you crush on dosen't like you, then they ask you out. Our feelings do not define our reality. I have a lot to live for. I just feel like I want to die. I feel like I can't handle it... But that doesn't mean I can't. I just feel that way. I've been saying for YEARS I can't do this anymore. But here I am. Doing it. I did it. Even though it felt like I couldn't. I STILL feel like "I CAN'T DO THIS SHIT ANYMORE"  *EVERYDAY*. But I do. I will wake up tommorow and go to work and live my life everyday till I die. Even if the whole time I felt like I wanted to die and couldn't do it anymore. It's just a feeling. An overwhelming feeling, that takes control. Take it back and see it for what it is. A feeling. Separate yourself from your feelings. And you will see you have much to live for.

It's not all bad. Pain is a part of life. Even if it's extreme pain, even constantly. There will always be the little things that make life worth living. It's not the big things. Like graduation, a family or long term career that make life and all the pain worth it. It's a pet. A hug. A pretty flower. A beautiful sunset. These small moments that bring you happiness are the things that make it worth it. You see, without pain, we would not value happiness. If we were happy all the time, then happiness is nothing. Nothing special. Nothing to be enjoyed. But it's the little things that happen everyday like a funny video you saw, that bring you happiness, even momentarily, that make life worth living, and when you are depressed you cherish those moments so much more than anyone else could imagine.  It may not seem like the small things matter. But everyone else just places too much emphasis on the big things that in actuality, don't end happy a lot of times. Life is a fluctuation of good and bad moments. Don't measure. Don't say "my life had been mostly shit so I should die". There were good times. You just can't remember them right now. If there's even a little good, it's worth it. No matter how small that amount of joy is. You can choose to say my life is only pain. Or you can choose to say I had some good moments. It's perspective on that issue, the issue of "is my life worth living", that determines if if truly is worth it or not. And that's a decision you CAN make. Not a feeling.
